ASTRO-USA Mini-Hab · Food Production Module

A digital model of an analog-habitat food production module

The ASTRO-USA Food Production Module is a converted shipping container that grows food for a simulated crew. This model rebuilds it from its published description and generates engineering CAD, airflow simulations and an interactive 3-D / VR walk-through from one sourced ledger, so a corrected input reaches every output.

The habitat

What the Food Production Module holds, as described by the ASTRO-USA team.

ASTRO-USA (Analog Simulation Training and Research Outpost Utilizing Self-sustaining Architecture) is an analog habitat being developed at Purdue University. Its first physical module, the Food Production Module (FPM), converts a shipping container (modelled as a 40 ft high-cube) into a growing space with a vertical nutrient-film (NFT) hydroponic wall, a propagation rack, Kratky and Dutch-bucket systems, a bay for bioreactor payloads, a battery bank and a work space, with the HVAC unit in an attic at the far end. It is designed to support a crew of 6 for a two-week mission (Peters et al., ICES-2026-251).

Analysis results

Airflow, heat and CO₂ from OpenFOAM, plus well-mixed models where they suffice.

Every simulation is a time-averaged transient run that must close its mass, heat, CO₂, water-vapour and age-of-air balances within 1 % and be statistically stationary before any value is used.

Validation: choosing the turbulence model

Against laser-Doppler measurements of the IEA Annex 20 ventilated-room benchmark, the standard k-ε model erred by 0.04–0.12 of the inlet velocity and SST k-ω by 0.07–0.18, so the habitat runs use k-ε.

The baseline airflow

The cold supply jet leaves the attic partition at ceiling height and falls to the floor part-way along the room; the two crew plumes are the warmest, highest-CO₂ air. The run closes its heat balance to +0.14 % and its CO₂ balance to -0.57 %.

Room-wide averages are robust: they change by at most 2.6 % across three meshes and 1.9 % between turbulence models. Single-point values are not (up to 13 and 25 %).

Occupancy and airflow

With six crew the room's CO₂ rise grows ×2.97. Halving the airflow raises the temperature rise ×2.35, CO₂ ×2.44 and the age of air ×2.26, more than the ×2 of a perfectly mixed room: the air-change efficiency falls from 0.50 to 0.44. The room mixes less well at low flow, not only less often, so the attic unit's airflow matters.

Where bioreactor off-gas should go

At the placeholder rate the bioreactor rack's CO₂ adds about 0.8 ppm mixed through the room, against about 88 ppm from two working crew; even ducted to the hydroponic wall it raises the canopy by only 1.1 ppm. At these rates it is neither a hazard nor a useful CO₂ supply for the plants.

to reach the bottom of that range. Either the lights sit outside the stated budget or the crop will be strongly light-limited.

If the HVAC fails

With the door shut and no air exchange, CO₂ reaches OSHA's limit (an eight-hour average) in about 2.1 h with six crew and 6.3 h with two. Leakage slows this a lot, so a door-shut CO₂ decay test is the measurement that settles it.

Where to put a room sensor

A wall sensor on the attic partition at 1.2 m stayed within 0.27 K and 4.9 % of the occupied-zone mean in all 4 runs, 1.6 m from the nearest growing system. Toggle "suggested sensor positions" in the 3-D model to see them.

Concepts

The ASTRO-USA plan, and how this model is built.

The Mini-Hab and the primary habitat

In the ASTRO-USA plan the Food Production Module is one of several modules of a secondary habitat, the Mini-Hab, alongside a Biosafety Level 2 Laboratory Module, Crew Quarters and NASA Kennedy Space Center's BioWaTERR wastewater-treatment trailer, which together aim to close the waste and nutrient loops; SIMOC Live and an Opto 22 system will monitor and control them. A primary habitat is envisaged as modular cylindrical and spherical sections in aluminium or titanium. Only the FPM is dimensioned in the paper; the other modules here are concept-level placeholders.

The generated concept encloses 488 m³ of pressurised volume (airlock excluded) for a crew of 6; it meets NASA's minimum net habitable volume of 25 m³ per person (Whitmire et al. 2014) once at least 0.31 of that volume is habitable.

One ledger, three models

Every dimension and load is a ledger record with its value, unit and either a source with a verbatim quote or a declared assumption with its reason; the build refuses anything else. A parts registry turns the ledger into three models, each with its own checks, so that replacing an assumption with a measured fact updates all of them.

  1. SourcesICES-2026-251 floor plan and text, container specification, NASA BVAD
  2. Ledger172 records: quoted, derived or declared assumption
  3. Parts registryevery part with its role in CAD, CFD and VR
  4. Engineering CADSTEP, STL, GLB, DXF drawings; floor-plan overlay gate
  5. Airflow CFDOpenFOAM cases; balance, stationarity and mesh checks
  6. VR scenethree levels of detail, navigation mesh, this browser viewer

What the team can supply next

82 assumptions can only be replaced by the ASTRO-USA team. The answers that unblock the most:

  1. Grow lights: fixture, count, wattage, photoperiod, and whether they are inside the power budget.
  2. Attic HVAC: make and model, airflow, grille positions, and whether it brings in outdoor air.
  3. Container leakage: a door-shut CO₂ decay measurement.
  4. The CAD model behind the paper's renders, to check this geometry against it.
  5. Bioreactor payloads: which hardware, with envelopes, gas ports and loads.

scenario_s5b.hvac.supply_flow600.0cfmS5 sensitivity screen: twice the M0 placeholder flow (300 cfm), supply temperature unchanged.
scenario_s6.bioreactor_rack_openTrue-The rack is an open frame: 10 tubes (~0.105 m3) fill ~27 % of its 0.391 m3 envelope, below the 0.6 fill fraction above which a part is modelled as a solid (review item 10). The model carries envelopes only, so the tubes are not drawn.
scenario_s6.enclosure_openTrue-yesThe bioreactor bay enclosure's walls, doors and ventilation are not described (Fig 4 shows a transparent box). With a solid block nothing inside it could exchange air, so S6 treats the bay as open to the room: an upper bound on mixing out of the bay.
scenario_s6.payloads_poweredTrue-S6 runs the payloads: the photobioreactor's LED heat and the bioreactor rack's off-gas CO2 are switched on.
scenario_s6.routes['bay', 'photobioreactor', 'nft_wall']-yesCandidate off-gas routes: (1) each vessel vent releases into the bay; (2) piped to the photobioreactor's sparger up to its maximum flow, the remaining vessels venting into the bay, culture uptake taken as zero (no rate for the placeholder), so the CO2 leaves at its vent; (3) ducted to the NFT canopy and released evenly through it.
sensors.exclusion_layers['plants', 'water', 'payloads']-Registry layers whose parts exchange gas or humidity with the air in reality but not (or not fully) in the current CFD.
sensors.exclusion_margin0.3mCandidates within this distance of a plant, water-culture, bioreactor-bay or payload part are dropped: plant and fungal gas exchange is not modelled yet (the canopy carries LED heat only), so the CFD would wrongly rate a sensor in or beside a canopy as representative of the room, whereas in reality it would read the plants.
sensors.mount_heights[1.2, 1.5]myesCandidate wall-mount heights: seated and standing breathing height, both reachable for maintenance.
sensors.occupied_zone_z[0.1, 1.8]mHeight band the crew occupy and breathe in (standing crew, 1.75 m tall in the crew ledger); the reference each candidate sensor is scored against is the volume mean over this band.
sensors.spacing0.25mSpacing of candidate positions along each wall; positions that fall inside equipment are dropped.
sensors.wall_offset0.05mSensor sampling point this far off the wall lining (housing depth).
site.crew_layout[{'item': 'bunk stack (2 berths)', 'wall'myesConcept berthing for the paper's crew of six (two-week mission): three two-berth stacks, lockers and a table. Illustrative only; galley, hygiene and medical spaces of Fig 1 are not yet placed.
site.lab_layout[{'item': 'sink + eyewash', 'wall': myesConcept arrangement of the equipment listed for the Lab and Work Area and the waste-management bioreactor train in Fig 1 (Year-2 Laboratory Module, BSL-2 intent). Positions and sizes are illustrative proportions for discussion only.
site.module_container20 ft standard dry-yesFig 10 draws the Laboratory and Crew Quarters modules at roughly half to two-thirds of the FPM's length; a 20 ft container is the nearest standard unit. Not stated in the paper.
site.row_gap0.0myesFig 10 draws the rows touching. A real site would leave access space between modules; replace with the planned spacing.
site.trailer.height3.5myesPlaceholder enclosed-trailer height; replace from ICES-2026-290 or the trailer itself.
site.trailer.width2.59myesTrailer dimensions are in ICES-2026-290 (not available); 102 in (2.59 m) is the usual US road-legal trailer width, used as a placeholder.
vr.battery_block[12.0, 6.8, 9.0]inyesVisual only: 16 x 12 V batteries (Fig 6) drawn as generic 12 V blocks (L x W x H); chemistry and model unknown.
vr.conduit_height2.35mVisual only: Fig 8 shows circuits running along both long walls to the rear panel; run height not stated.
vr.kratky_shelf_heights[1.0, 1.4]myesFig 5 render shows two wall shelves above the floor tub; heights not stated.
vr.kratky_small_bucket8.0inyesFig 5 render: small cube-shaped buckets, five per shelf; size not stated.
vr.nav_agent_radius0.25mWalkable-area (navmesh) margin around equipment: half a typical shoulder width, so a VR avatar or an engine character stays clear of what it would brush against.
vr.nav_head_clearance1.9mAn element blocks walking if its underside is lower than this (crew height 1.75 m in the crew ledger plus margin); higher items such as conduits are overhead.
vr.nft_channel{'width': 4.0, 'depth': 4.0, 'cup_diameter&#xinyesVisual only: Fig 4 shows 27 vertical columns of 11 planting holes; channel and net-cup sizes not stated.
vr.panel_center_height1.5mVisual only: breaker panel and disconnect mounting heights not stated.
vr.plant_radius{'nft': 0.11, 'seedling': 0.03, 'kratky'myesVisual only: plant canopy radii for leafy greens (NFT, Kratky), seedlings (propagation) and a vining crop (Dutch buckets); crops are not specified in the paper.
vr.receptacle_height18.0inVisual only: mounting height not stated; a common receptacle height is used.
vr.side_corrugation{'pitch': 0.278, 'depth': 0.036, 'flat_fractimVisual only: trapezoidal side-panel corrugation proportions typical of dry containers; not measured on the FPM's unit.
vr.solar_panel[1.76, 1.13, 0.035]myesVisual only: 10 panels totalling 4.4 kW nominal implies ~440 W each; drawn at a size typical of that class. Model, racking and tilt unknown.
vr.workbench_top_thickness1.5inVisual only.
